name: bot_whoami
description: Who you are as a Backplane bot: your name, id, home folder, rooms, routines, webhooks, and how deep the current conversation is.

name: bot_list
description: List the bots you can talk to: the bots on this machine (with what they are doing) and bots on linked machines (name@machine).

name: bot_send
description: Ask another bot for something, here (its name) or on a linked machine (name@machine). It goes in a room of the two of you named for `topic`, which the person can read: the same room each time for the same bots and topic, so every later message about a request stays together. It reaches the bot's inbox and waits while that bot works. Messages between bots carry a depth: each answer is one deeper than the message it answers, and after a few replies back and forth the next one is held (the person sees it, no bot hears it) until a person, a routine or a webhook starts a new exchange.

topic.description: What the request is about, in a few words; the room is named for it (default: the two bots' names).

direct.description: Send a private message instead of posting in a room. Only when the person asked for one.

name: room_list
description: List rooms (group conversations) and their members.

name: room_create
description: Make a room for a group of bots (you are added). Members are bot names here, or name@machine.

members.description: Members, separated by commas or spaces.

name: room_post
description: Post a message in a room: every other member hears it. Answer a post once, only when you have something to add; past the depth limit a post is held (the person sees it, no bot hears it).

name: room_read
description: Read a room's (or a direct conversation's) recent messages, oldest first.

room.description: The room's name or id, or a bot's name for your direct messages with it.

name: memory_save
description: Remember something, under a short key. Saving a key again replaces it: keep one current version of each thing, never a pile. Kinds: user (about the people you work for), pref (how they want things done), fact (the world, projects, contacts), howto (a procedure you learned), note (what happened; fades after a month). Save what will matter again; skip what won't.

key.description: A short key, e.g. user.timezone or howto.expense-report.

kind.description: user, pref, fact, howto or note.

text.description: What to remember, one or two sentences.

tags.description: Words that help find it later (optional).

name: memory_recall
description: Find what you remember about something: the best matches by key, tags and text.

name: memory_forget
description: Forget a memory that is wrong or no longer true.

name: memory_list
description: List everything you remember, newest first, optionally of one kind.

kind.description: user, pref, fact, howto or note (optional).

name: space_set
description: Set your space: your own UI, shown in your Space tab to people in Backplane (desktop, web and phone). A JSON document {title, blocks:[...]} with blocks of type heading, text, stat {label, value, hint}, progress {label, value 0..1}, list {items}, kv {rows [[k, v]]}, table {head, rows}, button {label, action}, input {label, action, placeholder}, divider, row {blocks}. A button or input sends you "[space] <action>: <value>". Keep it current: it is how people see what you are doing.

name: space_get
description: Read your current space (its JSON) and page (its HTML).

name: space_page
description: Set your space as a web page: HTML and CSS (inline <style> and style attributes), shown full screen in your Space tab on the phone apps in place of your blocks (desktop and web keep showing the blocks from space_set). No scripts run and nothing loads from the network: put images and fonts inline as data: URLs. A link to space:<action> works as a button; a form with action="space:<action>" and a field named value works as an input: both send you "[space] <action>: <value>". Other links open in the person's browser. At most 256 KB; an empty html removes the page.

name: routine_list
description: List your routines and reminders (scheduled prompts): kind (routine, once or reminder), when, the next time in the person's zone, and whether a one-time one is done.

name: routine_set
description: Make or change a routine: a prompt you receive on a schedule, or once. Give exactly one of `schedule` (every 15m, every 2h, daily 09:30, weekdays 08:00, @hourly, @daily, or a cron line: minute hour day month weekday) and `at` (one time: 2026-10-14T09:00, in 20m, in 2h, tomorrow 9am, monday 09:30, 17:30). Times are the wall clock of the person's time zone by default (daylight saving included), so 09:30 stays 09:30 wherever they are; `tz` picks another (a name like Europe/Helsinki, or person; machine = this machine's own offset). A one-time routine runs once, then stays in the list as done.

id.description: The routine to change (omit to make one).

tz.description: person (default for a new routine), a zone name, or machine.

prompt.description: What you will be asked each time.

name: routine_delete
description: Delete one of your routines or reminders.

name: project_list
description: List the person's projects (id, name, folder). Start work in one with thread_launch and its `project`; thread_list, thread_read, thread_send and thread_wait reach threads in any of them.

name: bot_create
description: Make a sub-bot: a new persistent bot (its own cat, memory and thread) for a lasting role you want to hand off, like watching a queue or owning an area. You are its maker. Bots made by bots go at most two levels deep, and each bot keeps at most eight. For one-off work start a thread with thread_launch and its `project` instead.

name.description: Its name: 1 to 24 letters, digits, - or _.

persona.description: Who it is and what it does, in a few sentences.

provider.description: claude, codex, grok, muse, antigravity, opencode, pi or omp (default: yours).

name: plane_read
description: Read the status plane as text: what waits on the person (approvals, questions, failures, most urgent first), what runs, the bots, the rooms with unread posts and the routines, here, with the ids thread_read and thread_send take. With `machine` (machine_list shows them), that other machine of the person's own plane instead, its ids made <link>~<id>. idle lists the day's idle threads too.

machine.description: Another machine's name (or link id): read its plane.

idle.description: Also list the threads idle in the last day (default: only their count).

name: notify_person
description: Alert the person on their phone and desktop. Allowed only for: needs_you (you are blocked until they decide, approve, log in, enter a code or answer; prefer asking in your turn's question or an approval when that fits), done (work the person gave you in your own thread is finished; at most once per thing they asked), reminder or digest (only in a turn that a routine they scheduled started). Anything else is refused: post it in a room, put it in your Space or on the task board, where it shows in the app without an alert.

text.description: What they should know, short: the first line is what the alert shows.

name: remind_person
description: Alert the person at a time, with no agent turn: a notification on their desktop and phone, and a reminder line in your thread. Use it for 'remind me...', not routine_set. Times as in routine_set's `at`, in the person's time zone unless `tz` says otherwise.

name: person_timezone
description: The person's time zone: with no `zone`, the zone, where it comes from (set, phone, machine), its offset and abbreviation now, and their local time now. With `zone` (a name like Europe/Helsinki; auto goes back to following their phone) it changes it.

name: project_create
description: Make a new project for the person: a folder (made when missing) added to their projects. The person is asked to approve it first. Answers the project's id; start work there with thread_launch and that `project`.

path.description: The folder: an absolute path, ~/x, or a name (under the home folder).

name.description: Its name in the sidebar (default: the folder's).
